[[Category:Vector space operation]]
Let $B_1=(\vec u_1,\dots,\vec u_n)$ and $B_2=(\vec v_1,\dots,\vec v_n)$ be [[vector space basis|bases]] of [[vector space]] $V$, and their corresponding [[matrix]] form

$$
\mathbf{B^1}=\begin{pmatrix}\vec u_1&\cdots&\vec u_n\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mathbf{B^2}=\begin{pmatrix}\vec v_1&\cdots&\vec v_n\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Then

$$
\exists ! \mathbf{P}_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}=\mathbf{B^2}^{-1}\mathbf{B^1} \\
\Rightarrow 
\forall \vec x \in V: [\vec x]_{B_2}=\mathbf{P}_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}[\vec x]_{B_1}
$$

$\mathbf{P}_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}$ is known as the '''transition matrix''' from $B_1$ to $B_2$.

Consequently,

$$
\mathbf{P}_{B_1\leftarrow B_2}=\mathbf{P}_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}^{-1}=\mathbf{B^1}^{-1}\mathbf{B^2}.
$$

<blockquote>
All bases of $V$ have the same dimension $n$.
</blockquote>

== Equivalent form ==

If

$$
\forall j \in \{1,\cdots,n\}: \vec u_j=\sum_{i=1}^n p_{ij}\vec v_i,
$$

then

$$
\mathbf{P}_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}=(p_{ij})
$$
